D12.title: Teaching compensation posting basis and contract supersession windows
questions: What does a teaching assignment's flat contract payable mean across recurring payroll periods, given that assignments are open-ended and every later period re-selects them?
How does revising an instructor contract affect the superseded contract's effective window, given that an open-ended predecessor made payroll match two contracts and refuse to run?
owner_answers: One-off payable: each assignment is compensated exactly once, in the first payroll period that covers it.
Close the old contract at the successor's start: the predecessor's effective_end becomes the day before the successor's effective_start.
authorizes: One Additional Salary per teaching assignment, posted in the first period that covers it and never again for that assignment.
A revision closes the predecessor's window the day before the successor starts, so exactly one contract covers any period and the successor rate applies from its own start date.
Assignments and adjustments already compensated in an earlier period are reported under already_compensated_prior_period rather than skipped silently.
does_not_authorize: Treating the flat amount as a per-period or pro-rated figure.
Retroactive application of a successor rate to periods already paid.
Rewriting any rate, term, quantity or adjustment on a superseded contract; historical compensation remains reproducible from it.
A second payroll engine, a parallel payable ledger, or any statutory/tax/slip calculation; native HRMS Salary Slip and Payroll Entry remain the payroll authority.
Production authorization; production remains REJECT.
D12.why_owner_only: Both are compensation semantics with direct financial consequences: one determines how many times a teacher is paid for one teaching fact, the other determines which rate applies from which date. Engineering failed both closed rather than guess, and both were escalated.

D13.title: Recovery objectives (RPO / RTO)
questions: What data loss and downtime can the business actually tolerate, so the capacity/availability gate has a real target instead of an unselected one?
owner_answers: RPO 24 hours, RTO 8 hours. Recover to the last nightly backup; tolerate up to roughly one day of lost enrolments and payments; restore service within eight hours.
D13.exact_scope: The local-server + Tailscale deployment currently selected. No internet-hosted topology is implied.
authorizes: Engineering to build and rehearse backup and restore against a 24-hour RPO and an 8-hour RTO, and to record measured results against those figures.
does_not_authorize: Does NOT authorize production. Selecting a target is an input to engineering, not evidence that the target is met; the corresponding D8 gate stays BLOCKED until it is independently proven.
Inventing availability, SLA or capacity numbers beyond these two figures.
Treating the targets as met because they are now written down.
D13.why_owner_only: RPO and RTO are business tolerances for lost tuition records and closed-door time, not engineering preferences. Section 12 forbids engineering from inventing them.

D14.exact_scope: Current launch backup destination is a separate local drive on the same computer. Off-site destination and custody are future scope and no device, site, vendor or address is selected.
authorizes: Engineering is authorized to complete and evidence the current local secondary-drive backup and restore. No off-site implementation is required at this stage.
does_not_authorize: Does NOT authorize or block production by itself. The current launch backup requirement is the separate-local-drive backup and its tested restore.
Treating future off-site/NAS/second-device backup as a current requirement.
Sending student data to a third-party cloud; any future off-site strategy requires a later explicit Owner decision.
D14.why_owner_only: Whether to require off-site custody is a business risk decision. The Owner has explicitly deferred it for the current launch.

D15.title: Production authorization scope
questions: Do you authorize production, and at what scope: local server + Tailscale only, full production including the internet edge, or not at all?
owner_answers: LOCAL LAUNCH ONLY. The local server + Tailscale deployment is the authorized launch scope. The public internet edge (provider, hostname, DNS, public edge) is NOT authorized and stays unselected.
D15.exact_scope: Deployment-scope authorization for the currently selected local-server + Tailscale topology only.
authorizes: The local server + Tailscale deployment as the launch target; the Owner runs the launch runbook there.
Engineering to build the D16 controlled production-activation path for the named production site.
Closing launch evidence (restore rehearsal, TLS/session checks) against the local scope only.
does_not_authorize: Does NOT flip production to GO while SEC-DEPS-01 is REJECT: the Owner's simultaneous standing decision keeps the dependency gate at REJECT until the findings can be read, so production_state stays REJECT.
Any internet deployment: no provider, hostname, DNS or public edge is selected or authorized.
Waiving the backup-restore rehearsal, TLS/session evidence, or durability/observability gates; scope authorization is not gate passage.
Treating hosted synthetic qualification as production evidence.
D15.why_owner_only: Only the Owner can accept the business risk of serving real students on the system and can bound where that risk may be taken. Engineering cannot authorize its own launch target.

D16.title: Production activation mechanism
questions: Do you authorize engineering to build a controlled production-activation path, given that every owned command currently refuses a non-synthetic site?
owner_answers: YES. Build the explicit, auditable activation: owned commands may operate on the named production site once the activation flags are present; everywhere else the synthetic-only hard stop stays in force.
D16.exact_scope: toefl_house.security site-mode resolution and the guarded command entry points only. Activation is the explicit triple: toefl_house_production_active=1 AND toefl_house_production_site equal to the running site name. Mixed synthetic+production mode is refused; the two qualification hostnames can never be the production site.
authorizes: Implementing site-mode resolution (SYNTHETIC / PRODUCTION / REFUSED) with fail-closed refusal as the default.
Accepting PRODUCTION mode at the guarded command entry points (authorize, require_command, and the domain entry guards) alongside unchanged SYNTHETIC qualification behavior.
Documenting the server activation steps in the launch runbook with verification commands.
does_not_authorize: Removing or weakening require_synthetic on any qualification path; synthetic behavior is unchanged.
Any activation that does not name the production site explicitly, or that activates a qualification hostname.
Production GO by itself; activation is a mechanism, and production_state stays REJECT until the gates close.
D16.why_owner_only: Lifting the synthetic-only hard stop changes what data the system may touch. Only the Owner can permit real student data to enter the command paths.

D17.title: Backup retention behavior
questions: Must every valid backup set be preserved forever, or may older valid sets be deleted beyond an Owner keep count?
owner_answers: Delete valid older sets beyond keep count. Owner selection recorded 2026-10-14; the exact runtime value is the Owner Configuration string 'Delete valid older sets beyond keep count'.
D17.exact_scope: Applies only to older backup sets that pass the existing SHA-256/size/manifest verification in the local secondary-drive backup flow. No backup set has been deleted under this decision yet.
authorizes: Recording 'Delete valid older sets beyond keep count' as the Owner-approved backup_retention_behavior when the Owner saves the Owner Operations policy in the ERP Configuration desk.
Engineering reconciliation of the implementation and docs that previously described the retention behavior as unresolved.
does_not_authorize: Any backup, deletion, restore or activation before the Owner enters the keep count (backup_retention_versions), nightly schedule time, ASCII-armored public recovery key and custody terms in Owner Configuration and a verified backup exists; backup and activation remain fail-closed until then.
Inventing the keep count or schedule values; they remain Owner-entered configuration, never defaults or code.
Production GO by itself; production_state stays REJECT until all gates close.
D17.why_owner_only: Deleting verified backups trades recovery history for disk use; only the Owner can accept that risk.

owner_answers: Add a Backup On/Off option in the Course Owner Configuration desk. Default and present requested state: Off. The Course Owner may turn it On later when needed.

Existing backup files and receipts remain untouched when turned Off. Turning On still requires verified owner policy, local separate-drive encrypted backup and independent restore/launch evidence.
authorizes: Implement a Course Owner-only On/Off control, default Off.
Refuse new TOEFL House product backup runs when the switch is Off without deleting any preexisting backup.
Invalidate prior backup receipt identity when the switch is turned On again.
does_not_authorize: Deleting or invalidating previously created backup files or Owner computer data.
Declaring production GO or using real student/finance records while required recovery acceptance is missing.
Bypassing D17 retention decision, backup schedules, public recovery key, separate-drive proof, real restore tests, other release gates, or emergency backup preservation.
